title: Remove version component from plugin path
description:
Remove the major.minor version from the plugin path, i.e:
        lib/plugins/X.Y/{epan,wiretap,codecs}
    and use an unversioned path:
        lib/plugins/{epan,wiretap,codecs}
    
    Introduce a new naming policy for plugins that requires
    name.so.ABI_VERSION.
    
    This is a simplified filesystem layoutfor plugins some
    important benefits such as:
    
     * improves compatibility between Wireshark versions, because
    a plugin that wasn't recompiled will be automatically picked
    up, but only if it has a compatible ABI version in the file name.
     * does not clash with Apple guidelines
     * simpler for users to understand and apply
     * just overall simpler and easier to maintain, removes a lot
    of complexity from CMake code
    
    It does impose more requirements on the plugin naming scheme
    but this should be handled completely transparently
    by the build system.
    
    It would also be possible to add support for unversioned *.so file
    extensions at the same time, although in ths case it is not possible
    to support multiple Wireshark ABI versions with only *.so, of course.
    This wasn't done here but it may or may not be a useful enhancement
    in the future.
    
    Follow-up to 90b16b40921b737aadf9186685d866fd80e37ee6.

This results in plugins named "<plugin>.so.<version>" on macOS and "<plugin>.dll.<version>" on Windows. macOS typically uses the format "<plugin>.<version>.so" and Windows typically uses "<plugin><version>.dll". We should probably use the conventional format on each platform, although I'd be OK with "<plugin>.<version>.dll" (with the extra ".") on Windows.

If I understand correctly you are saying `${_abi_version}` is having no effect on these platforms. OK, thank you, I will investigate it.

I did notice macOS uses a slightly different convention for .dylib shared libraries but since this is a plugin it didn't seem it mattered much but anyway, either way is fine with me.

As far as I can tell the plugins are loading fine, it's just that we're using a nonstandard file naming convention on macOS and Windows. I forgot that GitLab's editor eats <angle bracketed text> and fixed the markup; apologies for the confusion.

Ah OK now your point is more clear. :slight_smile:

That was intentional but I'm not a mac/Windows user. Do let me know if you'd like to change that and I can do it.

> I did notice macOS uses a slightly different convention for .dylib shared libraries but since this is a plugin it didn't seem it mattered much

The Finder appears to care, but `dlopen()` would be fine with a loadable module being called "module.rhinoceros", and the Finder's inability to recognize .so is hardly a major issue, so .so is fine.

The [Mach-O spec](https://web.archive.org/web/20090901205800/http://developer.apple.com/mac/library/documentation/DeveloperTools/Conceptual/MachORuntime/Reference/reference.html) says that

> The MH_BUNDLE file type is the type typically used by code that you load at runtime (typically called bundles or plug-ins). By convention, the file name extension for this format is `.bundle`.
> 
> The MH_DYLIB file type is for dynamic shared libraries. It contains some additional tables to support multiple modules. By convention, the file name extension for this format is `.dylib`, except for the main shared library of a framework, which does not usually have a file name extension.

but it appears that the distinction between those two types isn't significant; at minimum, `dlopen()` is fine loading an MH_DYLIB at runtime (we do that to libpcap.dylib in order to handle an API present in some OS versions but not others).

But, again, I'm not sure it's worth using `.bundle` for plugins (especially given that `.bundle` is also used for macOS bundles containing plugins, in which the `.bundle` is a directory with subdirectories such as Contents/MacOS, which contains the executable code file; that file has *no* extension).

> macOS typically uses the format "<plugin>.<version>.so"

Not as an OS convention for plugin names.

commits_data.title: Remove version component from plugin path
commits_data.message:
Remove version component from plugin path

Remove the major.minor version from the plugin path, i.e:
    lib/plugins/X.Y/{epan,wiretap,codecs}
and use an unversioned path:
    lib/plugins/{epan,wiretap,codecs}

Introduce a new naming policy for plugins that requires
name.so.ABI_VERSION.

This is a simplified filesystem layoutfor plugins some
important benefits such as:

 * improves compatibility between Wireshark versions, because
a plugin that wasn't recompiled will be automatically picked
up, but only if it has a compatible ABI version in the file name.
 * does not clash with Apple guidelines
 * simpler for users to understand and apply
 * just overall simpler and easier to maintain, removes a lot
of complexity from CMake code

It does impose more requirements on the plugin naming scheme
but this should be handled completely transparently
by the build system.

It would also be possible to add support for unversioned *.so file
extensions at the same time, although in ths case it is not possible
to support multiple Wireshark ABI versions with only *.so, of course.
This wasn't done here but it may or may not be a useful enhancement
in the future.

Follow-up to 90b16b40921b737aadf9186685d866fd80e37ee6.
